newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close mostly higher.

text.p: March 14 - IMM currency futures closed mostly higher, as dealers and funds continued to liquidate dollars ahead of the weekend. Traders said activity was surprisingly light given the sudden mid-morning rally in yen, marks. March contracts expire on Monday morning. They said U.S. PPI data dashed some expectations for higher U.S. rates.
June marks rose to $0.5948, near major resistance at $0.5953 or about 1.6900 spot marks, while June yen steadily extended the morning's gains towards resistance at $0.008237 or 123.00 spot yen.
Yen futures turned higher after Massachusetts Institute of Technology economist Rudi Dornbusch said he foresees dollar intervention once the dollar/yen spot rate hit the 130.00 to 135.00 area.
"The market took it as a significant comment, but when you read through it it didn't really mean that much," one currency trader said.
He noted that Japanese exporter selling knocked dollar/yen off its 124.00 perch, or about $0.008170 in June yen.

"He (Dornbusch) is good at the big picture," one forex trader said. However, the trader pointed out that Dornbusch's forecast was a private one and was not an indication of the U.S. administration's dollar policy.
He and other traders said the market's reaction to Dornbusch's comment reflected the underlying nervousness about the Group of Seven's dollar policy.
In addition, they noted that the dollar failed to rally out of its recent ranges even before the comments hit the tape.
"Everyone loaded up on dollars and when the dollar didn't rally through 1.71 (marks), they decided to test the currency on the downside," another trader said.
Most currencies held a firm tone after the U.S. February producer price index fell 0.4 percent, compared to average trade estimates for a decline of 0.1 percent.
The report lifted U.S. bonds and lowered U.S. yields.

However, even if U.S. yields continue to back off their recent highs, traders said the structural problems in Europe and speculation about a delay in the European Monetary Union (EMU) will drag down Continental European currencies.
June Canadian dollars turned lower after failing to test critical resistance at $0.7387.
March currency futures contracts expire on Monday, March 17 starting at 0915 CST/1515 GMT.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was up $0.000003 at $0.008211, marks were up $0.0046 at $0.5938, Swiss francs were up $0.0048 at $0.6930, sterling was up $0.0046 at $1.5988, Canadian dollars were down $0.0002 at $0.7370, Australian dollars were $0.0043 higher at $0.7968 and Mexican pesos were up $0.000600 at $0.120150.
